thread:
maya: Hi all — I threw together a tiny Next.js edge quickstart that wires the Redwood SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex for an eval POC. Running into weird auth/retry loops on SSR fetches. Anyone seen this?
kevin: Can you paste the exact error? Helps to know whether it's a 401 vs 403 vs SDK retry.
maya: It's intermittently 401 from /v1/generate when using the client in getServerSideProps. Logs show token refresh attempts: "token_refresh: failed, retrying". Using frontend SDK v0.8.2.
sam: That sounds like the browser token flow on the edge. We recommend doing a server-side exchange in an API route and passing a short-lived server token to the edge function.
maya: Hmm — I'm already calling /api/redwood-token but still seeing retries. Simplified code:
```
// pages/api/redwood-token.ts
import { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from 'next'
export default async function handler(req, res){
  const t = await getRedwoodServerToken();
  res.json({ token: t });
}
```
...and then in getServerSideProps fetch('/api/redwood-token') -> use client with that token.
kevin: Two possible issues: 1) edge vs node runtime mismatch (Edge API routes don't support some KMS libs), 2) SDK auto-retries detect transient 401 and try refresh which races with your manual exchange.
olivia: For the quickstart we should add a note: "use dedicated server API route (not Edge runtime) for key exchange". Also recommend locking SDK retry config: { retries: 0 } for SSR calls if you handle refresh yourself.
maya: That helped. I switched the API route to a standard Node serverless route, set retries:0 and it stopped the 401 churn. Still seeing occasional 429s for short bursts when running local eval harness.
sam: For 429s, enable simple exponential backoff on the eval harness runner and use batching. Also try fetchOptions: { keepAlive: true } for node HTTP agent when doing many sequential requests.
maya: Updated README in the repo with the server-token pattern + sample config. Pushing PR now. Anyone want to add a tiny eval test that verifies no client-side token usage in SSR? (low friction)
kevin: I'll add a basic jest/e2e that spins up the sample and asserts server route returns token and that page fetches data on server-side render. :thumbsup:
